'''Asakura Shrine''' (あさくらじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Saginomori Myōjin-chō, {{ill|Wakayama (city)|Q200747|qid=Q200747}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|Q131314|qid=Q131314}}. It is listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined Deity ===
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}}

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
The shrine’s early history is unknown. In the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}* *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}* from the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, it is recorded as “Asakura Shrine” in {{ill|Nagusa district|Q11415547|qid=Q11415547}}, {{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}, and is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. The *{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}* records it as “Asakura-no-Kami, Senior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade.”

According to the *Wakayama Prefecture Shrine Register* from the {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}, repairs to subordinate shrines were carried out in May of {{ill|Kankō|Q2736722|qid=Q2736722}} 2 ({{ill|1005|Q19231|qid=Q19231}}), with reconstructions recorded in May of {{ill|Eitoku|Q1145805|qid=Q1145805}} 2 ({{ill|1382|Q6335|qid=Q6335}}), April of {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} 18 ({{ill|1411|Q6155|qid=Q6155}}), December of {{ill|Eikyō|Q1193059|qid=Q1193059}} 10 ({{ill|1438|Q6377|qid=Q6377}}), August of {{ill|Kōshō|Q1143364|qid=Q1143364}} 3 ({{ill|1457|Q6518|qid=Q6518}}), and during the {{ill|Eishō (Muromachi period)|Q1193577|qid=Q1193577}} era ({{ill|1504|Q6148|qid=Q6148}}–{{ill|1521|Q6288|qid=Q6288}}). During warfare in the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} era ({{ill|1585|Q6736|qid=Q6736}}), the shrine lost its land holdings.<ref name="place-name"/>

In {{ill|Bunroku|Q1373039|qid=Q1373039}} 5 ({{ill|1596|Q6785|qid=Q6785}}), the Wakayama Castle deputy governor {{ill|Kuwayama Shigeharu|Q11537542|qid=Q11537542}} rebuilt the shrine. It was later destroyed by fire in {{ill|Manji (era)|Q1145295|qid=Q1145295}} 2 ({{ill|1659|Q6995|qid=Q6995}}), and restored the following year by the {{ill|Kishū Tokugawa family|Q11605046|qid=Q11605046}}.<ref name="place-name"/>

According to the “Saginomori Shrine Record” from {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 8 ({{ill|1723|Q6921|qid=Q6921}}), the location of the original Shikinaisha Asakura Shrine had become unknown. During the {{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}} era ({{ill|1673|Q7617|qid=Q7617}}–{{ill|1681|Q7645|qid=Q7645}}), a Confucian scholar of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wakayama Domain}}, Ri Baikei, identified the shrine—then called “Kenkoku-sha”—as the Shikinaisha and renamed it “Asakura Shrine.”<ref name="place-name">“Asakura Shrine” entry, *Place Names of Wakayama Prefecture*.</ref>

In the Meiji period, under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a Village Shrine. The shrine buildings were destroyed in the Wakayama air raids during World War II and were rebuilt in 1960.<ref name="place-name"/>

=== Court Rank ===
* Senior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade (as recorded in the *{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}*) — listed as “Asakura-no-Kami.”
